questions.title: Newton's law of gravitation — satellite orbit relation, geostationary height & angular speed

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The gravitational force between two point masses is directly proportional to the product of their masses, and inversely proportional to the square of their separation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
GMm/R² = mRω²
Substituting ω = 2π/T: GM/R² = R(2π/T)² = 4π²R/T², giving 4π²R³ = GMT²

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.answer:
The orbit is from east to west (rather than west to east).
The orbit is not equatorial (e.g. it is polar).

questions.title: Ideal gas — number & mass of molecules, r.m.s. speed & its temperature variation

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: An ideal gas is a gas that obeys pV ∝ T, where T is the thermodynamic (absolute) temperature.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: mass of one molecule = 0.0424/(1.27 × 10²⁵) = 3.34 × 10⁻²⁷ kg

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Sketch a line from (0, 0) to (500 K, v) with a decreasing positive gradient throughout (v ∝ √T).

questions.title: First law of thermodynamics — gas cycle & overall energy transfers

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: ΔU = q + W: the increase in internal energy of a system equals the work done on the system plus the energy transferred to the system by heating.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
A → B: change in internal energy decreases; work done on gas is positive.
B → C: change in internal energy increases; work done on gas is zero.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Over the whole cycle the change in internal energy is zero. More work is done by the gas in CD than is done on the gas in AB (no work is done in BC and DA), so overall the gas does work. There must therefore be an overall input of thermal energy.

questions.title: Oscillating sphere on a spring — frequency, acceleration & energy interchange

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer:
Comparing v = ±9.7√(11.6 − x²) with v = ±ω√(x₀² − x²) gives ω = 9.7 rad s⁻¹.
f = ω/2π = 9.7/2π = 1.5 Hz

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: x₀² = 11.6, so amplitude x₀ = √11.6 = 3.4 cm

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Sketch a straight line through the origin with negative gradient, passing through (+3.4 cm, −a₀) and (−3.4 cm, +a₀), with ends at x = ±3.4 cm.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The sum of potential energy and kinetic energy is constant. At maximum displacement the kinetic energy is zero and the potential energy is maximum; at zero displacement the kinetic energy is maximum and the potential energy is minimum.

questions.title: Two capacitors — charge sharing, final p.d. & energy decrease

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Q_A = CV

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: E_A = ½CV²

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Some of the charge transfers to the plates of capacitor B, because the p.d.s across the capacitors are not equal. The transfer stops when the p.d.s across the capacitors become equal.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
After sharing, V_A = V_B and the total charge is conserved: Q_A + Q_B = CV.
C V_B + 3C V_B = CV → 4C V_B = CV → V_B = V/4

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
Final total energy = ½ × 4C × (V/4)² = ⅛CV²
ΔE = ½CV² − ⅛CV² = ⅜CV²

questions.title: Magnetic flux & electromagnetic braking — disc e.m.f. & Lenz's law

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Magnetic flux is the product of the magnetic flux density and the cross-sectional area perpendicular to the magnetic field.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
Time for one revolution = 1/25 s.
e.m.f. = rate of cutting flux = ΔΦ/Δt = 0.069 × 25 = 1.7 V

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The induced current is perpendicular to the magnetic field and causes a force on the disc that <u>opposes</u> the rotation (Lenz's law). Applying Fleming's left-hand rule, the current is from the rim to the axle.

parts.answer: Full-wave rectification

parts.label: (a)(ii)

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.answer: Arrow drawn indicating the current in resistor R to the right.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Sketch a periodic curve with minimum V_OUT = 0 and maximum V_OUT = +V₀, showing peaks at t = 0, 0.5T, 1.0T, 1.5T and 2.0T, with V_OUT falling to zero halfway between each peak (a rectified sine shape).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Sketch a sinusoidal curve with troughs sitting on the time axis, peak power at t = 0, 0.5T, 1.0T, 1.5T and 2.0T, and zero power halfway between each peak.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: The r.m.s. values are the same, because the power dissipated (proportional to V²) does not depend on the sign of V, so the V²–time graph is identical for V_IN and V_OUT.

questions.title: Atomic energy levels — emission spectrum lines & level energy

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Each transition emits a single photon whose energy equals the difference in energy between the two levels. The frequency of the radiation corresponds to the photon energy (E = hf), so each transition produces one specific frequency.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Draw line A to the left of the existing pair, with a larger gap between A and the nearest line of the pair than between the two lines of the pair.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw line B to the left of both the existing pair and line A, with a larger gap between B and A than between A and the nearest line of the pair.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
E = hf, so E₂ = E₁ + hf_A and E₃ − E₂ = hf_B.
E₃ = E₁ + hf_A + hf_B = E₁ + h(f_A + f_B)

questions.title: Nuclear fusion — mass defect, energy released & stellar temperature

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Mass defect is the difference between the mass of the nucleus and the total mass of its nucleons when they are infinitely separated.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: neutron

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
Number of ⁴₂He nuclei formed per second = L/E = 1.4 × 10²⁸ / 2.8 × 10⁻¹² = 5.0 × 10³⁹ s⁻¹.
Mass of one ⁴₂He nucleus = 4 × 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ = 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
Mass per unit time = 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ × 5.0 × 10³⁹ = 3.3 × 10¹³ kg s⁻¹

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: electrons

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: The electrons are decelerated (stopped) on impact with the metal target; the kinetic energy lost by the electrons is emitted as X-ray photons.
